translations.text: ...to the king.
You are the wall-stone that the builders once rejected from the work.

It is well fitting for you that you should be the head of the glorious hall, and join together the wide walls, the unbroken flint, in a firm fitting, so that throughout the earthly [?] all with the sight of their eyes may wonder forever at the Lord of glory.
Reveal now through your skill your own work, true and bright with victory, and at once leave wall standing against wall.
Now the work has need that the craftsman should come, and the King himself, and then repair the house under its roof, now that it has fallen into decay.
He created that body, the limbs of clay. Now the Lord of life must rescue the weary host from the wrathful ones, the wretched from terror, as he has often done.
O Ruler and righteous King, you who keep the locks, who open life, the blessed ways on high, and refuse to another the beautiful longed-for journey if his work is not worthy.

Truly we speak these words out of need, and [?] remind him who created man that he not [?] let the cause of the sorrowful [?] come about, we who sit sorrowing in prison, hoping for the sun, waiting for when the Lord of life will reveal the light to us,

become a protector to our minds, and wrap our feeble understanding in glory, and make us worthy of that [glory] into which he admitted [them], when we had to turn in humiliation to this narrow land, cut off from our homeland.
Therefore he who speaks the truth can say that he rescued the first race of men when it had been ruined.
The woman was young, a maiden free of sin, whom he chose as his mother. That came about without a man's love, so that the bride became pregnant with the birth of a child.
Never was anything equal to it, before or since, in the world: the merit of a woman. That was hidden, the mystery of the Lord.
All spiritual grace sprouted across the face of the earth. There many teachings were illuminated, long-lasting lore, through the Author of life, teachings that had before lain hidden under darkness,
the songs of the prophets, when the Ruler came, he who enlarges the course of every utterance of those who often wish to praise the Creator's name in a wise manner.
O vision of peace, holy Jerusalem, best of royal thrones, city of Christ, native seat of angels, and in you alone the souls of the righteous always rest, exulting in glory.
Never shall a sign of stain be shown in that dwelling-place, but every sin, curse and strife shall turn far away from you. You are full of glory, of holy hope, as you are named.
Look now yourself around through this wide creation, and also at the roof of the sky, gaze widely on every side, how the King of heaven seeks you on his journey,
and comes himself, and takes up his dwelling in you, as wise prophets said in words long ago: they proclaimed the birth of Christ and spoke for your comfort, best of cities.

Now the child has come, born to bring relief from the labours of the Hebrews. He brings you bliss and loosens the bonds forced on you by enemies. He knows dire need, and how the wretched must wait for mercy.
O joy of women throughout the majesty of glory, most noble maiden over all the region of the earth of whom sea-dwellers have ever heard tell,
explain to us the mystery that came to you from the heavens: how you ever received the conception of a child through birth, and yet did not know intercourse in the manner of humans.
Truly we have never heard of such a thing happening in days of old, that you received such a thing as a special gift, nor need we expect that event to come again in time.

Indeed, a worthy faith dwelt in you, now that you bore the majesty of glory in your womb, and your great virginity was not corrupted. As all the children of men sow in sorrows, so afterward they reap: they bring forth to death.
The blessed maiden, ever full of victory, holy Mary, said: "What is this wonder that you marvel at, and lament, mourning with sorrows, son of Jerusalem together with its daughter?
You ask out of curiosity how I kept my maidenhood, my virtue, and also became mother of the glorious Son of the Creator.
That mystery is not known to men, but Christ has revealed in the dear kinswoman of David that the guilt of Eve is entirely cancelled, the curse cast away, and the humbler sex is glorified.
Hope has been received that now blessing may be shared by both, men and women, forever onward, to dwell always with the true Father in the heavenly joy of the angels."
O Earendel, brightest of angels, sent to men over middle-earth, and true radiance of the sun, bright above the stars, you always illumine every season from your own self!
Just as you, God born of God of old, Son of the true Father, always existed without beginning in the glory of heaven, so now your own creation, in its need, boldly begs you to send us the bright sun,
and to come yourself to enlighten those who long before, covered with smoke and here in darkness, sat in perpetual night; enfolded in sins, they had to endure the dark shadow of death.

Now we, full of hope, believe in salvation through the Word of God brought to the multitudes. In the beginning that Word was co-eternal with God, the Father almighty, and now in turn it has become flesh free of sins, which the virgin bore as help for the sorrowful.
God was seen among us without sins. The mighty child of the Creator and the son of man lived together in harmony among the people.
For this we may always give thanks to the Lord of victory, as is fitting, because he was willing to send himself to us.
O God of spirits, how wisely you were named with the right name, Emmanuel, as the angel first said it in Hebrew! That is interpreted in turn, fully according to its mysteries:

"Now the Guardian of the heavens, God himself, is with us." In this way the men of old long ago truly foretold the coming of the King of all kings, and also of the pure priest, just as the famous Melchizedek, wise in spirit, once revealed the divine majesty of the eternal Ruler of all.

He was the bringer of the law and the leader in teaching to those who had long hoped for his coming here, as had been promised them: that the Son of the Creator himself would cleanse the peoples of the earth, and would also seek out the depths on his journey by the power of the spirit.
Now they waited patiently in bonds for the time when the Son of God would come to the sorrowful. Therefore, struck down by torments, they spoke like this: "Now come yourself, high King of heaven.
Bring us the life of salvation, to us weary slaves of torment, overcome by weeping and by bitter, burning tears. The remedy rests entirely with you alone, for those in desperate need.

[Seek out?] the sad-hearted captives here [?]. When you turn from here, do not leave so great a multitude behind you, but show your mercy to us royally, Christ the Saviour, Prince of glory. Do not let the accursed ones have power over us.
Leave us the eternal joy of your glory, so that those whom you once made with your hands may worship you, glorious King of hosts. You dwell in the heights forever with the ruling Father."
"O my Joseph, son of Jacob, kinsman of David, the famous king, must you now break off our firm affection and abandon my love?"
"I am suddenly and deeply troubled, robbed of my honour, because on your account I have heard many words of great sorrow, grievous speech and injury. They speak scorn to me, many insulting words.
I must shed tears, sad at heart. God can easily heal the sorrow of my heart and comfort a wretched man. O young woman, maiden Mary!" "Why do you lament and cry out in sorrow?

"I have never found any fault in you, any cause for complaint, any sins committed, and yet you speak these words as if you yourself were filled with every sin and crime." "I have received too many sorrows from this pregnancy!
How can I answer hateful talk, or find any answer against the hostile?
It is widely known that I freely received from the Lord's bright temple a pure virgin, without stain, and now she is changed through someone [?].
Neither avails me, speaking or keeping silent. If I tell the truth, then David's daughter must die, stoned to death.
It is still worse if I conceal the crime: a perjurer must live on afterwards, hateful to every people, despised among the folk." Then the woman revealed the true mystery, and spoke thus:

"I tell the truth, by the Son of God, the helper of souls: I do not yet know any man anywhere, anyone on earth, through union. But it was granted to me, young in my home, that Gabriel, heaven's archangel, announced salvation to me.
[He] truly said that the Spirit of heaven had lit me with light, and that I was to bear the glory of life, a bright son, the mighty child of God, the radiant author of glory.
Now I have been made his temple without blemish; the Spirit of comfort has made his dwelling in me. Now put away all your bitter sorrow and care.

Give eternal thanks to the glorious Son of God that I became his mother, yet still a virgin, and that you are called his father in worldly opinion. The prophecy had to be truly fulfilled in him himself."
O true and peaceable King of all kings, Christ almighty, how you existed before all the glories of the world came to be, with your glorious Father, a child begotten through his skill and might!

There is no man now under the sky, no wise-minded person, so very clever that he could tell it to sea-dwellers and explain rightly how the Guardian of the heavens took you as his noble son in the beginning.

Of all the things that the races of people here have heard of among the nations as happening first, at the beginning under the clouds, it was this: that wise God, the source of life, divided light and darkness with lordly power,

and he had the power of judgment. Then the Lord of hosts gave this command: "Now let there be light from now on, forever and ever, a shining joy for each of the living who will be born in the generations to come."
And at once it happened, since it had to be so. Light shone for the tribes of people, bright among the stars, following the course of the seasons.
He himself ordained that you were his Son, dwelling together with your only Lord before anything of this world ever came to be.
You are the Wisdom who, together with the Ruler, made all this wide creation.
Therefore no one is so clever or so skilled in mind that he could clearly show your origin to the children of men.
Come now, Guardian of victory, Creator of mankind, and graciously show your mercy here!
All of us need to know your mother's lineage, the true mystery, now that we cannot explain your father's lineage any further at all.
Gracious one, bless this world by your coming here, Saviour Christ, and the golden gates, which in days of old had long stood locked,
high Lord of the heavens, command them to be opened, and then come to us, humble, on your own journey to earth. We need your mercies!
The cursed wolf, the beast of dark deeds, has scattered your flock, Lord, and driven it far and wide.
What you, Ruler, once bought with your blood, the evil one harshly oppresses and takes captive, against the longing of our need.

Therefore, Saviour, we pray to you earnestly with the thoughts of our hearts that you quickly bring help to the weary exiles, so that the slayer who brings torment falls, humbled, into the depths of hell,
and your handiwork, Creator of men, may rise and rightly come to the noble kingdom on high, from which the dark spirit once drew us away and led us astray through sinful desire,

so that we, deprived of glory, must suffer misery forever without end, unless you, eternal Lord, living God, protector of all creatures, will rescue us all the more quickly from the destroyer of the people.

O glorious one of the world, purest queen over the earth of all who have ever been, how rightly all who have speech, men throughout the earth, call you and say with joyful hearts that you are the bride of the best Lord of heaven.

Likewise the highest in the heavens, Christ's servants, also say and sing that by holy powers you are lady of the glorious host, and of the earthly orders under the heavens, and of the dwellers in hell.
For you alone of all people resolved gloriously, with bold intent, to bring your virginity to the Lord and give it without sin.
No other like you has come, none above all people, a bride adorned with rings, who has since sent such a bright offering with a pure heart to the heavenly home.

Therefore the Lord of victory commanded his high messenger to fly here from his mighty majesty and quickly make known to you the abundance of his powers: that through a pure birth you would bear the Son of the Lord as a mercy to people, and that you, Mary, would remain spotless forever after.
We have also heard that long ago, in days of old, a truthful prophet, Isaiah, said of you that he was led so that he saw the whole dwelling-place of life in the eternal home.
Then the wise prophet looked out across the land until he gazed upon the place where a noble entrance had been set.
The whole immense door was bound with precious treasure and wrapped with wondrous bands. He firmly believed that no man could ever, in all eternity, raise such fast bolts,
or unlock the bar of the city gate, until God's angel, with a gracious mind, revealed the matter to him and spoke these words:
"I can tell you something that has come true: that at some time God himself, the Father almighty, will yet cleanse these golden gates with the power of the Spirit,
and through the fast locks seek the earth, and then after him it shall stand eternally, ever and always so closed that no other, except God the Saviour, shall ever again unlock it."
Now that has been fulfilled which the wise man then looked upon there with his eyes.
You are that door in the wall; through you the ruling Lord journeyed out once onto this earth, and Christ almighty found you just so, adorned with powers, pure and chosen.
So after himself the Lord of angels, the giver of life, locked you again with a limb-key, unblemished in every respect.
Show us now the grace that the angel, God's messenger Gabriel, brought to you.
Indeed, the city-dwellers pray that you make known that comfort to the peoples: your own son. Then we may all hope with one mind, now that we gaze upon the child at your breast.

Intercede for us now with bold words, that he no longer let us obey error in any way in this valley of death, but that he bring us into the Father's kingdom, where we may afterwards dwell without sorrow in glory with the God of hosts.
O holy Lord of the heavens, long ago you existed together with your Father in the noble home.
No angel had yet been made, nor any of that great and mighty host who watch over the kingdom up in the heavens, the Prince's glorious dwelling and his service,
when you were first with the eternal Lord, yourself establishing this wide creation, the broad and spacious lands. The high Spirit, the sure protector, is shared by you both.
We all pray to you humbly, Savior Christ, that you hear the voice of the captives, your bondservants, saving God, and how we are afflicted through our own will.
The cursed spirits, those exiles, the hateful ravagers from hell, have hard oppressed us and bound us with cruel ropes. Our remedy depends entirely on you alone, eternal Lord.
Help the sorrowful, so that your coming here may comfort the wretched, though through the lust of sins we have committed hostility against you.
Have mercy now on your servants and think of our miseries, how we stagger with feeble minds and wander about in humiliation. Come now, King of men, do not delay too long.
We have need of your kindness, that you rescue us and, true as you are, give us the gift of salvation, so that from now on we may always thrive among the people in the better things, your will.

O beautiful one, full of honors, high and holy heavenly Trinity, blessed far and wide across the spacious plains! Those who have the gift of speech, the wretched people of the earth, should rightly praise you on high with all their strength, now that God the Savior, true to his pledge, has revealed to us that we may know him.

Therefore the righteous race of seraphim, eager in deed and strengthened in glory, up among the angels, ever proclaiming, sing with untiring majesty, very loftily, with loud voice, beautifully far and near.

They have the finest of offices with the King. Christ granted them that they might enjoy his presence with their eyes forever and without ceasing, adorned in heaven, and worship the Ruler far and wide.

and with their wings they guard the face of the almighty Lord, the eternal Lord, and press eagerly around the throne of the prince, each striving to be the one who can fly nearest to our Saviour in the courts of peace.
They praise the beloved one and speak these words to him in the light, and glorify the noble origin of all creation:
"Holy are you, holy, Lord of archangels, true Lord of victory; you are ever holy, Lord of lords! Your glory on earth endures forever among men in every age, honored far and wide.

You are the God of hosts, for you have filled earth and heavens with your glory, protector of warriors, guardian of all creatures. To you be eternal salvation in the highest, and praise on earth, shining among men.
Blessed are you, beloved one, who came in the Lord's name to the multitudes as a comfort to the lowly. To you in the heights be eternal praise forever, without end."

Lo, that is a wondrous exchange in the life of men, that the merciful Creator of mankind received undefiled flesh from a maiden, and she knew nothing of a man's love; nor did the Lord of victory come over the earth through any man's seed.

But that was a greater power than all the earth's people could understand as a mystery: how he, the glory of the skies, the high Lord of the heavens, brought help to mankind through his mother's womb.
And so, continuing onward, the Saviour of peoples, the Lord of hosts, deals out his forgiveness every day as a help to men.

Therefore, eager for glory, let us praise him faithfully in deeds and words. That is lofty counsel for every person who has understanding, that he should always worship God most often, most inwardly, and most eagerly.

The hallowed Savior himself will repay him the reward for that devotion, in the homeland where he never came before, in the joy of the land of the living, where he will dwell in bliss afterward and live forever without end. Amen.
